title: KV: page-tiling allocator and spillback hysteresis to reduce fragmentation and spill thrash
author: Arjun Patel
release_notes: Introduces a page-tiling KV allocator and a spillback hysteresis/rate-limiter to reduce memory fragmentation and spill thrashing; exposes tuning knobs under kv.page_* feature flags.
description: Context: On mixed inference workloads we observed pathological spillovers and large working-set fragmentation during bursty token generation (ENG-2173). This PR introduces a new page-tiling allocation layer and a spillback hysteresis controller to reduce external fragmentation, smooth spill events, and improve tail latency under constrained memory.
commits: a7f3d9c: introduce page_tiler module and fixed-size page allocator
c4b1aa1: add spillback_rate_limiter and integration with evictor/scheduler
f2e7b88: telemetry, benchmarks, docs and feature gating (kv.page_tiling, kv.spill_hysteresis)
perf_summary: Microbenchmarks + internal canary: 8-18% lower steady-state resident set size (workload dependent), 15% lower P99 latency on a mixed chat+completion workload with modest memory pressure, and ~30% reduction in spill events during synthetic burst tests. End-to-end cost metric improved due to fewer disk spill IOs.
rollbacks_and_flags: Feature gated behind kv.page_tiling and kv.spill_hysteresis. Default: enabled for dedicated infra canary only. Rollback: set kv.page_tiling=false and kv.spill_hysteresis=off or revert the config; evictor behavior returns to previous path. No DB schema changes.
review_thread: Maya Kline: Nice direction. Can we add a simple invariant test that ensures pages are not oversized relative to tenant quotas?
Author (Arjun): Added page_size cap and unit tests; updated tests/kv/page_tiler_test.rs to cover quota edgecases.
Diego Ruiz: The rate limiter looks good but I worry about latency spikes when the limiter kicks in. Can we expose a soft/hard threshold?
Author (Arjun): Exposed hysteresis window config (kv.spill_hysteresis.window_ms) and added a soft throttle path that reduces eviction aggressiveness before enforcing full spillback.
Hannah Chen: CI flake in bench harness fixed by making the synthetic workload seed deterministic. Approving after green CI.
ci_details: CI: unit, integration, lint, and bench-stability. One flaky bench test failed initially (timing nondeterminism) and was rerun; all checks passed on rerun. Bench harness added deterministic workload seed to avoid future flakes.
risk_assessment: Low-medium. New allocator adds a single extra indirection per allocation but is optimized for common paths; feature gated and off by default for hosted tier until canary completes. Monitoring added: kv.page_fragmentation_ratio, kv.spill_events, kv.spill_rate_limiter_trips.
changelog_entries: Performance: KV page-tiling allocator and spillback hysteresis reduce memory fragmentation and spill thrash under bursty workloads. Config knobs: kv.page_tiling, kv.page_size, kv.spill_hysteresis.*.
notes: This PR is part of a broader effort (ENG-2190) to stabilize mem pressure behavior across the serving runtime. Follow-ups planned: adaptive page sizing based on workload telemetry and scheduler prioritization of 'hot pages'.
